requirements.evidence: Data model, policies, routes and pages are present: migration adds owner_seq `storedAs("case when `role` = 'owner' then 1 else null end")` + unique `entity_memberships_one_owner` (create_entity_memberships_table.php:19-23); EntityPickController aborts 403 before touching the session and logs on `Log::channel('audit')` (EntityPickController.php:16-26); Settings uses `#[Locked] public int $entityId` and transfer checks owner vanished/target admin/not caller inside DB::transaction (Settings.php:18-19,77-117); dashboard hides settings link with `@can('manageSettings')` (dashboard.blade.php:11-13). Gap: Members::assignRole (Members.php:75-97) never refuses the owner's membership, so assignRole(ownerId,'employee') leaves the entity with zero owners, breaking the 'exactly one owner' invariant; Settings::delete is not atomic (Settings.php:63-64).

conventions.evidence: No app/Actions classes for domain writes (addMember/assignRole/removeMember/save/delete/transfer all write Eloquent directly in components); Livewire validation uses `Validator::make(...)` (Members.php:48-51,86-89) and inline `$this->validate([...])` with untyped, unattributed `public $name; public $slug; public $targetMembershipId;` (Settings.php:21-25) instead of `#[Validate]`; addMember/assignRole authorize with hand-rolled `abort(403)` role checks (Members.php:42-46,79-83) instead of policies; no tests (TDD convention). Positives: policies registered (AppServiceProvider.php:30-31), $fillable set, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG updated, x-form-field/x-button reused.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes server-side and resolves IDs scoped to the entity (`EntityMembership::where('entity_id', $entity->id)->findOrFail($membershipId)`, Members.php:91,105); entity id is #[Locked]; output escaped with {{ }}. But EntityMembershipPolicy::assignRole (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:17-22) and Members::assignRole allow an admin to change the owner's role, so an admin can strip the owner of ownership (and settings/billing control) via a crafted `assignRole(ownerMembershipId, 'employee')` call — an unauthorized privileged write.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files at all: no Pest tests for migrations/owner uniqueness, policies, entity.pick, or the Livewire actions, and no unauthorized-call or tamper tests required by the Livewire policy.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct code. Some redundancy: Dashboard/Members re-query the #[Locked] Entity model on every render (`Entity::query()->findOrFail($this->entity->id)`, Dashboard.php:27; Members.php:33-36); duplicated role checks `in_array($caller->role, [UserRole::Owner, UserRole::Admin], true)` repeated across policies and components instead of reusing the policies; UserRole::manageable() exists but assignRole hardcodes `Rule::in(['admin','employee'])` (Members.php:88).

readability.evidence: Clear names and small methods. Nits: rambling three-line comment in Settings::transfer (Settings.php:102-105); unused duplicate lang keys `owner_notice` and `transfer_property` (lang/en/ui.php, lang/pt_BR/ui.php); Settings stores an int id while sibling components store a locked model.

scope.evidence: All files serve the task (models, policies, migrations, factories, components, views, routes, lang, docs, changelog); no onboarding, switcher, middleware or navbar work added.

issues.explanation: No tests ship with the change, violating the mandatory TDD convention and the Livewire definition of done (unauthorized-call and tamper tests per action).
assignRole does not refuse the owner's membership, so an admin can demote the owner to employee/admin, leaving the entity with no owner and taking over control.
Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, save, delete, transfer) are done inline in components instead of app/Actions classes that authorize internally.
Public input properties lack #[Validate]; validation uses Validator::make / inline rules instead of the project pattern.
addMember/assignRole authorize with hand-rolled role checks and abort(403) instead of a policy ability (e.g. EntityPolicy::update).
Membership deletion and entity soft-delete are not wrapped in a transaction, so a failure can leave a half-deleted entity.
Migration filenames with 000001/000002 suffixes suggest hand-written rather than make:migration-generated migrations.
Unused duplicate keys `owner_notice` and `transfer_property` add dead translations.
Rambling comment restating the check adds noise.

review.summary: The change implements the entities data model with a portable single-owner constraint, policies, the pick endpoint and the Dashboard/Members/Settings Livewire pages, with docs and changelog updated. However it ships no tests at all, lets an admin demote the owner via assignRole (breaking the single-owner invariant), and skips the project's Actions and #[Validate] conventions, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
